subject: Activation scope & data-loss threshold: multi-region switchover exception request
messages:
From: Ian Walker <ian.walker@finvault.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: activation scope and data-loss threshold for multi-region switchover

Hi Neha,

Following up from our SRE sync this morning — FinVault is evaluating Redwood for our cross-region failover between EU and US. A couple of constraints came up from our side that we'd like to have captured in an SLA carveout rather than a general statement. Specifically:

- We cannot guarantee continuous replication under our peak ingest windows (end-of-day batch between 02:00-03:30 UTC), which may introduce short windows where RPO stretches to ~5 minutes for bulk batches.
- We need an activation lead time of 45–60 minutes for full warm-standby activation because a manual step is required in our IAM and network path on our side.

Can Redwood support a provisional exception that: (1) RTO for EU->US switchover is 60 minutes during the first 90 days of go-live, and (2) RPO for bulk batch windows may be up to 5 minutes?

We're happy to provide the replication/ingest profile and a high-level runbook (attached). Procurement will need a one-page addendum for redlines.

Thanks,
Ian
Ian Walker
Head of Platform Ops, FinVault
ops@finvault.com

Attachment: finvault-recovery-profile.pdf (PDF, 480KB)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ian Walker <ian.walker@finvault.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-28T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: activation scope and data-loss threshold for multi-region switchover

Ian —

Thanks for the detail and for attaching the replication profile. We can accommodate a scoped carveout during an initial stabilization window, but we need to align on operational controls and acceptance criteria first. High level proposal from our side:

- Provisional SLA addendum (90 days): RTO = 60 minutes for EU->US region failover.
- Allowed RPO variance: up to 5 minutes during documented bulk ingest windows; outside of those windows we expect sub-60s replication.
- Activation lead time and responsibilities: FinVault to perform IAM/network activation (we can provide a checklist); Redwood will complete model/container readiness and health validation.

We need the following items before we can finalize the addendum:
1) Confirm the ingest window schedule and expected batch sizes (timings in UTC).
2) A signed operational checklist showing FinVault's manual activation steps.
3) Agreement on an acceptance test (we propose a staged failover runbook execution in a non-production slice).

Karthik — can you draft a provisional SLA addendum and a short DRA template (2–3 pages) we can send to FinVault? Grace and I will loop in legal/procurement after we have the draft.

Ian — attaching our template will speed things up.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-dra-template.docx (DOCX, 115KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ian Walker <ian.walker@finvault.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-29T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: activation scope and data-loss threshold for multi-region switchover

Ian / Neha —

I've reviewed FinVault's replication profile. A few technical clarifications and a proposed mitigation approach:

- During the 02:00–03:30 UTC bulk window, we see spikes where continuous streaming falls back to micro-batching on some models due to write-amplification. That maps to the 3–5 minute RPO you observed.
- We can tighten effective RPO by enabling short-lived prefix caching for critical traffic (adds ~5% memory overhead) — this requires a config change and a 30-minute rolling restart on the serving pool.
- For activation lead time, Redwood can automate container warm-up and KV hydration in parallel while FinVault performs IAM/network changes; the combined time should be ~30–40 minutes on our side if the checklist is followed.

Proposed acceptance test (staged, non-prod slice):
1) Simulate bulk ingest for 40 minutes at expected rates.
2) Trigger controlled failover; measure RPO and end-to-end time to full traffic acceptance.
3) Validate state reconciliation and telemetry (latency, token-cost, error-rate).

I'll attach a 2-pager DRA with the automations flagged. If FinVault signs off on the checklist, I can produce the provisional SLA addendum with the carveout language (applies for the first 90 days post go-live).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Eng Manager, Runtime — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ian Walker <ian.walker@finvault.com>, procurement@finvault.com
Date: 2026-05-03T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: activation scope and data-loss threshold for multi-region switchover — proposed addendum

Team —

Summary and ask for approval to proceed with a provisional carveout:

What we're proposing to FinVault (provisional, 90-day stabilization):
- RTO (EU->US switchover): 60 minutes. This is contingent on the operational checklist being completed by FinVault before an incident.
- RPO: up to 5 minutes tolerated during the documented 02:00–03:30 UTC bulk ingest window; outside of that window, RPO target remains <60s.
- Redwood will implement prefix caching for critical traffic and provide a one-time config change with a 30-minute rolling restart.
- Acceptance test: staged failover on non-prod slice as outlined by Karthik.

Next steps we need approved internally:
1) Legal to sign the provisional-sla-addendum (attached) with the carveout language.
2) Operations to schedule the staged acceptance test with FinVault (tentative date: week of May 10).
3) Solutions to validate FinVault's manual IAM/network checklist and sign-off.

Jonas / Grace — please confirm if Legal can approve the language in the attached provisional-sla-addendum and whether the 90-day window is acceptable from a risk standpoint. If yes, I'll send to procurement and get DocuSign moving.

Thanks —
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachment: provisional-sla-addendum.pdf (PDF, 45KB)
